```fd
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 block
title "Alert-forwarding chain"

node probe "Probe"
node normalizer "Normalizer"
node sink "Sink"

# Waypoints (60,20) and (90,40) requested to jog this edge around a future
# third element, but via=/points=/path were WITHDRAWN with no replacement
# (MIGRATIONS 0.1): author waypoints are outside FigDown's stable
# surface. Edge draws under auto layout instead; the jog cannot be stated.
edge probe -> normalizer
edge normalizer -> sink
```

Notes on the fix:

- `block` is the **genre** name on line 1, not a node-declaration keyword — the validator rejected it as a directive. Scene elements use `node id "Label"`; once `probe`, `normalizer`, and `sink` exist as declared nodes, the two `edge` lines resolve their endpoints (that's why "unknown endpoint" also went away).
- `via=(60,20),(90,40)` is a hard error with no replacement spelling: waypoint routing was withdrawn from the language entirely (renamed to `points=`, then withdrawn along with `path`, per MIGRATIONS/core §9 OQ-S37). Per "Do not invent syntax," I didn't approximate it with some other key — I removed it and left a `#` comment at the point of doubt recording that the jog was requested but is not expressible, so a host document/reader can see the gap rather than silently losing the requirement.
- The other edge and both node labels are otherwise unchanged from your intent; nothing stated in the figure was deleted to force a pass — only the one construct the language does not have.

This should now build clean; the one thing to flag in the host document's prose is that the probe→normalizer edge draws straight under auto layout rather than jogging, since FigDown currently has no way to state that waypoint.
